explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are triploblastic organisms possessing a true middle germ layer (mesoderm), whereas coelenterates (cnidarians) are diploblastic.

options.c: has a mouth, tapeworm feeds by suckers

subject: Biology

explanation: Photoperiodism—the physiological response of plants to the relative lengths of day and night (duration of sunlight)—is the primary environmental trigger for flowering.

subject: Biology

options.B: has a reduced stem and thick fleshy leaves
options.D: bears many buds at the nodes
options.b: has a reduced stem and thick fleshy leaves
options.d: bears many buds at the nodes

explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll and therefore cannot manufacture their own food via photosynthesis, forcing them to obtain organic nutrients saprophytically or parasitically.

subject: Biology

subject: Biology

explanation: The hepatic portal vein transports nutrient-rich, deoxygenated blood directly from the gastrointestinal tract and spleen to the liver for processing.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)

explanation: In birds (Aves), gaseous exchange takes place across the walls of tiny air capillaries branching from the parabronchi within the lungs, while air sacs act only as bellows.

subject: Biology

explanation: During anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) in yeast and plants, pyruvic acid is decarboxylated and reduced to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

subject: Biology
question: The excretory organ in insect is the
explanation: Insects excrete nitrogenous wastes (primarily uric acid) and regulate water balance using slender Malpighian tubules attached to the junction of the midgut and hindgut.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)

explanation: Structure 5 opens directly into the hair follicle and secretes sebum to lubricate the hair and skin surface, identifying it as the sebaceous gland.

subject: Biology

explanation: Part 2 represents the Malpighian layer (stratum basale/spinosum) of the epidermis, where melanocytes synthesize melanin and keratinocytes actively divide and produce keratin.

explanation: The atlas is the first cervical vertebra (C1) that articulates directly with the occipital condyles of the skull, supporting the head and allowing nodding motion.

subject: Biology
question: Which enzymes are contained in the pancreatic juice?
explanation: Pancreatic juice secretes pancreatic amylase (digests starch), pancreatic lipase (digests fats), and trypsinogen/trypsin (digests proteins) into the duodenum.

subject: Biology

explanation: In standard JAMB synovial joint diagrams, label 3 points to the solid shaft/epiphysis of the articulating bone forming the joint.

subject: Biology

options.B: formation of a fertile embryo and the endosperm
options.b: formation of a fertile embryo and the endosperm

explanation: In angiosperms, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form the diploid zygote (embryo), while the second fuses with the polar nuclei to form the triploid nutritive endosperm.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)
question: In mammalian development, the function of the yolk is to

options.B: act as a shock-absorber to the foetus
options.D: facilitate the process of excretion in the foetus
options.b: act as a shock-absorber to the foetus
options.d: facilitate the process of excretion in the foetus

explanation: Although reduced in placental mammals, the yolk sac provides early nourishment to the developing embryo before the placenta becomes fully functional.

subject: Biology
question: Hypogeal germination is characterized by the

options.A: emergence of the plumule out of the ground
options.B: provision of nourishment by the endosperm
options.a: emergence of the plumule out of the ground
options.b: provision of nourishment by the endosperm

subject: Biology
topic: B7. Reproduction in Plants and Mammals

explanation: Parthenocarpic fruits (such as bananas and pineapples) develop from an unfertilized ovary and are consequently seedless.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is true of a climax community?

options.A: It persists until the environment or climate changes.
options.B: It changes drastically from one year to the next.
options.C: It is the first stage in succession.
options.D: It is made up of the tallest trees and the smallest animals.
options.a: It persists until the environment or climate changes.
options.b: It changes drastically from one year to the next.
options.c: It is the first stage in succession.
options.d: It is made up of the tallest trees and the smallest animals.

explanation: A climax community is the final, stable, self-perpetuating stage of ecological succession that remains in equilibrium unless disrupted by major climatic or environmental shifts.

subject: Biology
question: A population is defined as a collection of similar organisms that

options.C: are found in the same habitat
options.c: are found in the same habitat

explanation: In ecology, a population consists of individuals of the same species living in a given area at the same time that are capable of interbreeding freely to produce fertile offspring.

subject: Biology
topic: C2. Symbiotic Interactions, Energy Flow, and Nutrient Cycling
question: In a typical predator food chain involving secondary and tertiary consumers, the organisms become progressively

options.A: smaller and more numerous along the food chain
options.B: equal in number and size along the food chain
options.C: larger and fewer along the food chain
options.D: parasitized along the food chain as consumers get bigger
options.a: smaller and more numerous along the food chain
options.b: equal in number and size along the food chain
options.c: larger and fewer along the food chain
options.d: parasitized along the food chain as consumers get bigger

explanation: Because energy is lost at each trophic transfer (about 90%), higher trophic levels support fewer individuals, and predators generally need to be larger to capture their prey.

subject: Biology
topic: C1. Abiotic and Biotic Factors Affecting Distribution of Organisms
question: [DIAGRAM NEEDED: Aquatic pyramid of numbers/energy with four trophic levels labeled E (base) through H (apex)] Which level of the pyramid has the least total stored energy?
explanation: Level H is the apex (top trophic level) of the pyramid; due to progressive energy loss as heat at every trophic step, the top level retains the least stored energy.

subject: Biology
topic: C3 & C4. Natural Habitats and Local (Nigerian) Biomes
question: [DIAGRAM NEEDED: Aquatic food pyramid showing Algae at the base, Tadpole, Tilapia, and Shark at the top] Which organism in the pyramid functions as a tertiary consumer?
explanation: In the aquatic food chain Algae (producer) -> Tadpole (primary consumer) -> Tilapia (secondary consumer) -> Shark, the shark occupies the tertiary consumer level.

subject: Biology
question: Mangrove swamp can be found

options.A: on a seashore with flat terrain
options.B: where a river meets the sea
options.C: on a mud flat near the sea
options.a: on a seashore with flat terrain
options.b: where a river meets the sea
options.c: on a mud flat near the sea

explanation: Mangrove swamps thrive in brackish estuarine zones where freshwater rivers meet salty seawater, experiencing regular tidal flooding.

subject: Biology
question: Soil with the finest particles is called
explanation: Clay consists of mineral particles less than 0.002 mm in diameter, making them the finest soil particles with high water-retention capacity.

options.C: the invasion of the red blood cells by the trophozoites
options.D: the development of merozoites into gametocytes

explanation: Crossing homozygous dominant ($RR$) with heterozygous ($Rr$) yields gametes $R$ and $R$ from the first parent and $R$ and $r$ from the second, giving a 1:1 ratio of $2RR : 2Rr$.

topic: B9. Co-ordination, Sense Organs, Hormones, and Homeostasis

explanation: The appearance of a recombinant phenotype combining red fur from one parent and short ears from the other shows that the two traits assort independently and are not linked.

subject: Biology
question: Pawpaw seeds collected from a tree with many desirable agronomic qualities did not give rise to plants of desirable characters as the parent because

options.A: seeds are not reliable for propagating plants
options.B: uncontrolled out-crossing can introduce unwanted variability
options.C: vegetative propagation is the best form of reproduction for all crops
options.D: seeds were not physiologically mature at harvest
options.a: seeds are not reliable for propagating plants
options.b: uncontrolled out-crossing can introduce unwanted variability
options.c: vegetative propagation is the best form of reproduction for all crops
options.d: seeds were not physiologically mature at harvest

explanation: Sexual reproduction in pawpaw frequently involves cross-pollination from unknown pollen sources, introducing genetic recombination and variation that dilute parent traits.

subject: Biology
topic: D2. Heredity, Chromosomes, Probability, and Sex-Linked Characters
question: Women do not suffer from colour blindness

options.C: the genes are recessive and sex-linked
options.D: the genes occur on both the X and Y chromosomes
options.c: the genes are recessive and sex-linked
options.d: the genes occur on both the X and Y chromosomes

explanation: Red-green colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome, so females rarely express the condition because a normal dominant allele on their second X chromosome masks it.

subject: Biology
question: The hereditary material of the cell is
explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all cellular organisms.

subject: Biology
topic: C1. Abiotic and Biotic Factors Affecting Distribution of Organisms
question: An example of plant adaptation to a xerophytic environment is represented by the development of

options.B: broad canopy and extensive surface root system
options.D: rough leaves and shallow root system
options.b: broad canopy and extensive surface root system
options.d: rough leaves and shallow root system

explanation: Xerophytes conserve water in arid habitats by storing water in succulent, fleshy stems or leaves and reducing leaf surface area (often to spines) to minimize transpiration.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following factors is LEAST likely to affect the animals living in a freshwater habitat?
explanation: Freshwater habitats naturally have consistently low salt concentrations, so salinity fluctuations rarely act as a limiting factor compared to turbidity, temperature, or pH.

subject: Biology
question: The theory of natural selection was developed by
explanation: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace independently formulated the theory of evolution by natural selection, jointly presenting their findings in 1858.

subject: Biology
topic: E1 & E2. Theories and Evidence of Evolution
question: Fossil records found in sedimentary rocks offer some explanation for the theory of evolution because

options.A: the deposits have remains of organisms characteristic of when they were formed
options.B: different strata have remains of organisms of the same kind
options.C: only organisms with strong parts are fossilized
options.D: most animals and plant fossils bear little resemblance to present day living specimens
options.a: the deposits have remains of organisms characteristic of when they were formed
options.b: different strata have remains of organisms of the same kind
options.c: only organisms with strong parts are fossilized
options.d: most animals and plant fossils bear little resemblance to present day living specimens

explanation: Successive sedimentary rock strata preserve fossils in chronological sequence, demonstrating progressive changes in organism complexity over geological time.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following structures is associated with aerobic respiration?
explanation: Mitochondria are the organelles responsible for cellular aerobic respiration and ATP production.

subject: Biology

explanation: Ribosomes (or rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes) are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell.

explanation: Spermatophyta (seed-bearing plants) comprises gymnosperms (naked seeds) and angiosperms (flowering plants with enclosed seeds).

question: Which of the following are non-green plants?
explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll and cannot carry out photosynthesis, obtaining nutrients heterotrophically as saprophytes or parasites.

subject: Biology

explanation: Hydra (a coelenterate/cnidarian) possesses specialized stinging cells (cnidoblasts/nematocysts) on its tentacles for defense and capturing prey.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)

explanation: Pteridophytes (such as ferns) are vascular plants possessing true roots, stems, and leaves, unlike algae and bryophytes.

subject: Biology

explanation: Breathing roots (pneumatophores, as in mangroves) bear numerous pores called lenticels above waterlogged soil to allow oxygen entry for respiration.

subject: Biology

explanation: As the thick-walled cells of the annulus dry out and contract, tension ruptures the sporangium wall and catapults spores into the air for dispersal.

subject: Biology
topic: A1. Living Organisms: Characteristics, Cell Structure, and Levels of Organization

explanation: Hair-like cilia covering the body beat rhythmically to propel Paramecium through water and sweep food particles into its oral groove.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)

explanation: The clitellum is a glandular saddle-like band around segments 32–37 that secretes mucus and forms the cocoon enclosing fertilized eggs.

subject: Biology
question: The function of maxillipeds in crayfish is to aid
explanation: Maxillipeds are thoracic appendages modified as mouthparts that hold, manipulate, and shred food toward the mandibles.

subject: Biology
question: The respiratory organ in the land snail is the
explanation: In terrestrial pulmonate snails, the vascularized lining of the mantle cavity functions as a lung for gaseous exchange.

subject: Biology
question: The structure labelled 4 is for
explanation: Newly hatched tadpoles possess external gills for gaseous exchange (respiration) in water before internal gills and lungs develop.

subject: Biology
question: As the tadpole develops, the structure labelled 5
explanation: During metamorphosis, the tadpole's tail is gradually resorbed by phagocytosis and becomes shorter until it disappears in the adult toad.

subject: Biology
question: The gill rakers of fishes take part in
explanation: Gill rakers project forward from the gill arches to strain food particles from water and prevent solid debris from damaging the delicate gill filaments.

subject: Biology
topic: B1. Internal Structure of Flowering Plants and Mammals

explanation: Monocot roots such as maize possess a large central pith surrounded by a ring of alternating xylem and phloem bundles, unlike dicot roots (sunflower, bean, okra) which have a central star-shaped xylem without pith.

subject: Biology
topic: C1. Abiotic and Biotic Factors Affecting Distribution of Organisms
question: Which of the following is formed immediately after the first product of photosynthesis?
explanation: Simple sugars (glucose) produced first during photosynthesis are rapidly condensed into insoluble starch for temporary storage in the leaf.

subject: Biology
topic: B1. Internal Structure of Flowering Plants and Mammals
question: [Dissection showing the Abdominal Cavity of a rat — small intestine] In the digestive system, absorption of nutrients into the blood takes place in the part labeled
explanation: Digested nutrients are absorbed across the villi of the small intestine (ileum) into blood capillaries and lacteals.

subject: Biology
topic: B9. Co-ordination, Sense Organs, Hormones, and Homeostasis
question: [Dissection showing the Abdominal Cavity of a rat — pancreas] The gland which produces trypsin, amylase and lipase is labelled
explanation: The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice containing trypsinogen (trypsin), pancreatic amylase, and lipase into the duodenum.

subject: Biology
topic: B1. Internal Structure of Flowering Plants and Mammals

explanation: The liver (along with the pancreas and salivary glands) is an accessory digestive organ that secretes bile to emulsify fats in the small intestine.

subject: Biology
topic: A1. Living Organisms: Characteristics, Cell Structure, and Levels of Organization
question: The element common to protein, carbohydrate and lipid is
explanation: Carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins all contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen; nitrogen, sulphur, and phosphorus are absent from simple carbohydrates and neutral fats.

subject: Biology
topic: A2b. Evolution & Classification: Animalia (Invertebrates and Vertebrates)

explanation: Enamel is the hard, mineralized outer layer covering the exposed crown of a mammalian tooth to protect against wear.

subject: Biology

subject: Biology

explanation: Reduced atmospheric humidity steepens the water vapour concentration gradient between the leaf air spaces and surrounding air, accelerating transpiration.

subject: Biology
topic: B3. Transport System in Plants and Animals

options.c: be the same in X and Y

subject: Biology
topic: B3. Transport System in Plants and Animals

explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules from a dilute solution (higher water potential) to a more concentrated solution (lower water potential) through a semi-permeable membrane.

subject: Biology
question: Fibrinogen and prothrombin play important roles in the
explanation: During blood clotting, prothrombin is converted into thrombin, which catalyzes the conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads that trap blood cells.

subject: Biology
topic: B3. Transport System in Plants and Animals
question: Deoxygenated blood flows into the right and left lungs through the
explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the right and left lungs for oxygenation.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a plant excretory product?
explanation: Resins (along with tannins, alkaloids, gums, and latex) are metabolic by-products stored or excreted by plants, whereas cytokinin is a plant hormone.

subject: Biology
topic: C7. Humans and Environment (Diseases, Pollution, and Conservation)
question: The movement of the whole organism to an external stimulus is termed
explanation: Taxis (taxic movement) is a directional locomotory movement of an entire motile organism toward or away from an external stimulus such as light or chemicals.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following vertebrae lacks a centrum?
explanation: The atlas (first cervical vertebra) lacks a centrum and neural spine, forming a ring that accommodates the odontoid peg of the axis for nodding head movements.

subject: Biology
question: The function of the epididymis in mammals is the
explanation: The epididymis is a tightly coiled tube behind each testis where spermatozoa mature and are stored prior to ejaculation.

subject: Biology
question: A collection of achenes formed from several carpels of a flower is
explanation: An aggregate fruit (etaerio of achenes, e.g., strawberry or buttercup) develops from an apocarpous gynoecium with multiple free carpels in a single flower.

subject: Biology
question: Epigeal germination can be found in
explanation: Groundnut (a dicot) exhibits epigeal germination in which elongation of the hypocotyl pushes the cotyledons above the soil surface, whereas maize, sorghum, and millet are hypogeal.

subject: Biology
question: A dwarf plant can be stimulated to grow to normal height by the application of
explanation: Gibberellins stimulate rapid stem internode elongation and can overcome genetic dwarfism in plants.

subject: Biology
question: The greatest contribution to genetic studies was made by
explanation: Gregor Mendel established the foundational laws of inheritance (segregation and independent assortment) through his quantitative pea-plant breeding experiments.

subject: Biology
topic: D2. Heredity, Chromosomes, Probability, and Sex-Linked Characters
question: The exchange of genes between homologous chromosomes is called
explanation: Crossing-over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis, creating new genetic combinations.

subject: Biology
